// Non-blocking (hit-under-miss, multiple outstanding misses) write-back D-cache.
// Architecture:
//   * Set-associative tag/data arrays (flip-flop based).
//   * A file of MAX_MISSES miss registers ("MSHRs"). Each holds one missing
//     line address, at most ONE pending load (id+word) and at most ONE merged
//     store word (word+data+mask)  [C4-compliant: no per-miss line buffering].
//   * Loads to a line with a pending miss attach to its miss register and are
//     answered when the fill lands; stores merge into the register's store
//     word and are acknowledged immediately (store response data is free).
//   * One fill buffer (a single line) and a single outstanding memory
//     transaction (M3). Victim selection happens AFTER the fill data arrives,
//     so while a fill is unserved no cache line is "doomed": every resident
//     line keeps answering hits (C2). A dirty victim is written back after
//     the fill and before the install; during that short window, stores that
//     hit the victim line are redirected into a miss register so no store is
//     ever lost, and loads of it are still served from the array.
//   * Round-robin miss-register service order guarantees forward progress.
//   * Responses go through a small FIFO; rsp_valid is a register output and
//     never depends combinationally on rsp_ready (R1b).
